description: Implement the mcp-client crate: stdio + HTTP/SSE transports (P3.1), server lifecycle with initialize handshake / capability negotiation / list-tools / on-demand invoke / bounded reconnect-with-backoff / teardown and a per-server McpServerHandle (P3.2), tool discovery + schema mapping from MCP ToolDescriptors into providers::ToolSpec namespaced by server e.g. filesystem__read_file (P3.3), plus per-tool timeouts, output-size caps, structured tool-error results, and hiding tools from disconnected servers (P3.6, the mcp-client-side portion). Because this adds crates.io deps (tokio, serde/serde_json, thiserror, async-trait, reqwest for HTTP/SSE, futures/futures-util/bytes, rustls with ring, plus a JSON-RPC layer built in-crate), the crate MOVES from [workspace] members to [workspace] exclude and gains explicit CI steps. Includes a bundled CROSS-PLATFORM mock/fixture MCP server (spawned over stdio) and the mcp-client test suite. This is the foundation the orchestrator-core bridge (FEAT-002) builds on.
steps: Rewrite hybrid-orchestrator/crates/mcp-client/Cargo.toml with concrete version LITERALS (NOT {workspace=true}, since it becomes an excluded crate). Add: path deps domain={path="../domain"} and providers={path="../providers"} (for ToolSpec/ToolCall types); serde={version="1",features=["derive"]}, serde_json="1", thiserror="2", async-trait="0.1", tokio={version="1",features=["full"]} (need process, io, sync, time, macros, rt-multi-thread), futures="0.3", futures-util="0.3", bytes="1". For the HTTP/SSE transport reuse the EXACT providers reqwest setup: reqwest={version="0.12",default-features=false,features=["json","stream","rustls-tls"]} and rustls={version="0.23",default-features=false,features=["ring"]}. Set package version/edition/license as concrete literals (0.1.0 / 2021 / MIT) mirroring providers/Cargo.toml's header comment explaining why {workspace=true} cannot be used. Add a header comment mirroring providers/Cargo.toml explaining the exclude arrangement.

In hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml: MOVE "crates/mcp-client" from the [workspace] members array to the [workspace] exclude array (keeping routing as the sole remaining offline member). Update the explanatory comments in that file to reflect that mcp-client is now excluded and why (crates.io deps: tokio/serde_json/reqwest/rustls-ring/JSON-RPC stack unreachable offline), mirroring the existing per-crate exclude bullets and the EXIT PATH note. Also record any NEW dep versions in the [workspace.dependencies] documentation table if not already present (they are documentation only for excluded crates).

Implement mcp-client/src/transport/mod-level JSON-RPC types: a small in-crate JSON-RPC 2.0 layer (request with id/method/params, response with result/error, notification) using serde_json. Define a Transport trait (async: send a JSON-RPC request and await the correlated response; receive server->client notifications) that both transports implement. Derive Debug on all types tests will {:?}-format.

Implement mcp-client/src/transport/stdio.rs (P3.1): spawn the server as a child process via tokio::process::Command from McpTransport::Stdio{command,args,env}, speak JSON-RPC over the child's stdin/stdout (newline-delimited JSON per line, the common MCP stdio framing), read responses on a background task correlating by request id, and forward notifications. Handle child exit / broken pipe as a transport error. Cross-platform: use tokio::process (works on Windows + Unix); do NOT use Unix-only shell invocations.

Implement mcp-client/src/transport/http_sse.rs (P3.1): connect to McpTransport::HttpSse{url,headers} over HTTP for client->server JSON-RPC POSTs and consume Server-Sent Events for server->client streaming. REUSE the providers pattern: call the equivalent of providers::crypto::ensure_crypto_provider() BEFORE constructing any reqwest client (replicate the same ring-install-once pattern in this crate via a small crypto module OR depend on providers and call providers::ensure_crypto_provider), build reqwest::Client with the rustls-tls stack, and reuse an SSE decoder analogous to providers::capability::sse_event_stream (buffer bytes, split on blank-line frames, extract data: payloads). Apply the configured headers to requests.

Implement mcp-client/src/session.rs (P3.2): define McpConnectionState (or reuse orchestrator-core's if a dependency cycle is avoidable; if not, define an internal state enum in mcp-client and map at the bridge). Implement McpServerHandle holding: server id, McpServerConfig, connection state, negotiated capabilities, cached Vec of ToolDescriptor. Implement connect/spawn that: performs the MCP `initialize` handshake (send protocol version + client capabilities, receive + store server capabilities), then `tools/list` to cache ToolDescriptors, transitioning state Connecting->Connected. Implement invoke(tool, args) -> sends `tools/call` JSON-RPC and returns the result or a structured error. Implement bounded reconnect with backoff (capped retries, increasing delay via tokio::time) that marks the handle Disconnected on give-up. Implement teardown (graceful shutdown / kill child for stdio). Refresh tools on reconnect.

Implement mcp-client/src/tools.rs (P3.3): define ToolDescriptor (name, description, input_schema: serde_json::Value) deserialized from MCP tools/list. Implement namespacing: a namespaced tool name is `{server_name_or_id}__{tool_name}` (double underscore separator per Section 5.4 example filesystem__read_file). Provide functions to (a) convert a ToolDescriptor into providers::ToolSpec via ToolSpec::function(namespaced_name, description, input_schema), and (b) parse a namespaced tool name back into (server, tool). Guard against collisions: two servers exposing the same bare tool name get distinct namespaced names; document/handle the case where a server name itself contains the separator.

Implement P3.6 mcp-client-side resource handling in session.rs/tools.rs: per-tool invocation timeout (tokio::time::timeout, configurable with a sensible default) that yields a structured tool-error result (NOT a panic/crash) on elapse; output-size cap on tool results that truncates or errors when exceeded; and a `visible_tools()` accessor on the handle/registry that EXCLUDES tools from servers whose state is Disconnected (hidden from new requests per Section 5.6).

Rewrite mcp-client/src/lib.rs: remove the placeholder() fn and its smoke test; declare the modules (transport{stdio,http_sse, jsonrpc types}, session, tools); add ergonomic pub use re-exports (ALPHABETICALLY ORDERED) of the public API the orchestrator-core bridge and tauri-app will use (e.g. McpServerHandle, ToolDescriptor, transport traits, error types, namespacing helpers, the ToolSpec-conversion fn). Add crate-level doc comment mirroring providers/lib.rs explaining the exclude + CI-verification arrangement. NOTE: orchestrator-core/src/lib.rs's smoke test calls mcp_client::placeholder() - update that call site as part of FEAT-002 (leave a note); if it must stay compiling standalone here, keep a thin item or coordinate. Prefer: replace the placeholder reference in orchestrator-core smoke test in FEAT-002.

Add a bundled CROSS-PLATFORM mock/fixture MCP server for stdio tests. Structure it as either (a) a separate [[bin]] target in mcp-client that implements a minimal MCP server (reads JSON-RPC line-delimited on stdin, responds to initialize/tools/list/tools/call on stdout) so tests spawn it via env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name>") or std::env::current_exe with an arg switch, OR (b) a #[cfg(test)] helper that re-invokes the test binary in a mock-server mode. It MUST run identically on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest (no shell, no Unix-only syscalls; account for .exe on Windows). Document the chosen approach in a comment.

Write the mcp-client test suite (unit + integration under tests/ or #[cfg(test)] as fits): (1) full stdio round-trip against the bundled mock server: initialize handshake succeeds + capabilities stored, tools/list discovery returns expected ToolDescriptors, a tools/call round-trips a result. (2) tool-name namespacing collision test: two servers with a same-named bare tool produce distinct namespaced ToolSpec names, and reverse-resolution maps each back to the correct server. (3) argument-schema validation failure is captured as a structured tool-error (validation may live here or in the bridge - place the schema-validation-failure coverage wherever the validation is implemented; if validation is bridge-side, cover the transport/invoke error path here and note schema-validation is covered in FEAT-002). (4) per-tool timeout yields a structured error, not a hang/crash. (5) disconnected-server tools are hidden from visible_tools(). Use tokio::test. Derive Debug where tests {:?}-format.
acceptance_criteria: hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml lists mcp-client under [workspace] exclude (not members); `cd hybrid-orchestrator && cargo build --workspace` still succeeds offline (now building only routing) and does NOT attempt to resolve mcp-client's crates.io deps.
mcp-client/Cargo.toml uses concrete version literals (no {workspace=true}) and reuses the providers reqwest+rustls-ring feature set for the HTTP/SSE transport.
The stdio transport spawns a child via tokio::process (cross-platform; no Unix-only shell); the bundled mock MCP server is spawnable on both Linux and Windows.
Tool names are namespaced server__tool (double underscore) and reverse-resolvable; ToolDescriptor -> providers::ToolSpec conversion uses ToolSpec::function.
Per-tool timeout and output-size cap are implemented and yield structured tool-error results, not panics; visible_tools() excludes disconnected servers' tools.

The mcp-client test suite is written covering: stdio handshake + discovery + tools/call round-trip, namespacing collisions, timeout->structured error, disconnected-server hiding (schema-validation-failure covered here or deferred to FEAT-002 bridge with a note). Full compile/test/clippy is CI-deferred (crates.io deps unreachable offline).
verification: cd hybrid-orchestrator && cargo build --workspace  (must stay green offline with mcp-client excluded)
cd hybrid-orchestrator && cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/mcp-client/Cargo.toml --check  (must pass offline)

COMPILE/TEST/CLIPPY of mcp-client is CI-deferred: cargo build/test/clippy --manifest-path crates/mcp-client/Cargo.toml (-D warnings) run on ubuntu-latest + windows-latest via the CI steps added in FEAT-002. Note in findings which checks ran offline vs deferred to CI.
findings: IMPLEMENTED (all steps): (1) Rewrote crates/mcp-client/Cargo.toml with CONCRETE version literals (no {workspace=true}) mirroring providers/Cargo.toml's header rationale; path deps domain + providers; serde/serde_json/thiserror/async-trait/tokio(full)/futures/futures-util/bytes, and the EXACT providers reqwest(default-features=false, features=[json,stream,rustls-tls]) + rustls 0.23(default-features=false, features=[ring]) setup. Added a [[bin]] target `mcp-mock-server` (src/bin/mock_server.rs). (2) Root hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml: moved crates/mcp-client from [workspace] members to [workspace] exclude (routing is now the sole offline member); updated the explanatory comments, the per-crate exclude bullet, the EXIT PATH note, and the [workspace.dependencies] doc note. Cargo.lock now drops the mcp-client entry (correct for an excluded, previously-dependency-free member). (3) In-crate JSON-RPC 2.0 layer in src/transport/jsonrpc.rs (JsonRpcRequest/Response/Notification + untagged JsonRpcMessage demux by id). (4) src/transport/mod.rs defines the async Transport trait (request/notify/next_notification/shutdown). (5) src/transport/stdio.rs: tokio::process::Command spawn (cross-platform, no shell, .exe-aware), newline-delimited JSON framing, background reader task correlating responses by id via a oneshot pending-map and forwarding notifications over an mpsc channel; EOF/broken-pipe fails pending requests as TransportError::Closed. (6) src/transport/http_sse.rs: reuses providers pattern - own src/crypto.rs::ensure_crypto_provider() ring-install-once, reqwest rustls-tls client, headers applied, and a decode_sse_data_frames() decoder analogous to providers::capability sse handling. (7) src/session.rs: McpServerHandle with internal McpConnectionState (redefined here, NOT depending on orchestrator-core, to avoid the cargo cycle since orchestrator-core depends on mcp-client; kept in sync with orchestrator_core::McpConnectionState for the FEAT-002 bridge to map); connect() does initialize handshake (stores server capabilities) + tools/list (caches ToolDescriptors) Connecting->Connected; invoke() sends tools/call; reconnect() is bounded with exponential backoff via tokio::time and marks Disconnected on give-up; teardown() kills the child/drops transport. (8) P3.6: per-tool timeout via tokio::time::timeout and an output-size cap both yield STRUCTURED ToolResult{is_error:true} (never panic); visible_tools() returns [] unless Connected (hides disconnected servers' tools). (9) src/tools.rs: ToolDescriptor (camelCase inputSchema), namespacing server__tool with double-underscore (namespaces by server UUID id so reverse-resolution is unambiguous even if display name contains __), to_tool_spec() via providers::ToolSpec::function, resolve_namespaced() splits on FIRST separator. (10) src/lib.rs: removed placeholder()+smoke test, declared modules, ALPHABETICALLY-ORDERED pub use re-exports, crate doc mirroring providers. (11) Bundled cross-platform mock server (std-only, blocking IO + thread::sleep) with echo/slow tools; spawned in tests via env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_mcp-mock-server"). (12) tests/stdio_roundtrip.rs (#[tokio::test]) covers: stdio handshake+capabilities+discovery+tools/call round-trip, namespacing collision across two servers with reverse-resolution, unknown-tool JSON-RPC error captured as structured tool error, per-tool timeout->structured error (not hang), disconnected-server hiding (with cache retained). Unit tests also live in jsonrpc.rs/tools.rs/http_sse.rs/session.rs. OFFLINE-VERIFIED: `cd hybrid-orchestrator && cargo build --workspace` succeeds and (via -v) compiles ONLY `routing` (mcp-client is not resolved); `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/mcp-client/Cargo.toml --check` passes. Files are LF. Proactively fixed a clippy::or_fun_call risk (unwrap_or -> unwrap_or_else with allocating constructor). CI-DEFERRED (crates.io deps unreachable offline, HTTP 403): full `cargo build/test/clippy --manifest-path crates/mcp-client/Cargo.toml` on ubuntu-latest + windows-latest; the CI ci.yml step ADDITIONS for mcp-client are FEAT-002's job. ACTION REQUIRED FOR FEAT-002 (flagged, intentionally NOT changed here to keep FEAT-001 scoped to mcp-client): orchestrator-core/src/lib.rs line 58 smoke test still calls `mcp_client::placeholder()`, which no longer exists - FEAT-002 MUST update that call site (e.g. reference mcp_client::McpServerHandle) or orchestrator-core's standalone CI build will fail.
